newsitem.title: USA: Calif. Treasurer calls for calm over tax measure.
newsitem.headline: Calif. Treasurer calls for calm over tax measure.

text.p: California state Treasurer Matt Fong accused opponents of a controversial tax measure Thursday of overstating claims that the municipal bond market would be adversely impacted by its passage.
Proposition 218, which will appear on the November ballot, would limit the authority of local governments to impose taxes and property-related assessments, fees and charges.

"It's wrong for people to say the market will come crashing down or that bondholders will not be paid if Proposition 218 is passed," Fong said. "Political statements like that are irresponsible and negatively affect the market."
Fong said the U.S. Constitution protects the holder of bonds that are secured by a pledge of taxes, assessments, fees or charges.
A voter-adopted initiative is subject to the same federal constitutional limitations as a statute enacted by the Legislature, Fong said.
"Revocation of existing tax, assessment, fee or charge that would result in a bond payment default would surely be an impairment of contract forbidden by the Constitution," Fong said in a statement.
Fong said he does not believe that bondholder security would be impacted.

"Opponents of Proposition 218 should argue the merits of the initiative rather than claim that the sky will fall on bondholders if 218 passes," Fong said. "To fuel such speculation and concern is irresponsible and self-serving."

Stone & Youngberg LLC and other municipal finance firms have warned of the implications of the initiative. Stone & Youngberg recommended that its clients vote against the measure because of the "devastating effect the initiative will immediately have on local government finance."
